headline: Two American Airlines planes clip wings before takeoff at Reagan airport
author: Rebecka Pieder

paragraphs.text: Two American Airlines jets hit each other at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport while taxiing for departure in Washington DC on Friday.
One jet "clipped the wing" of the other at around 5:10 ET (22:10 GMT), the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement. No injuries were reported, and the FAA plans to investigate.
Both aircraft returned to the gate and were removed from service to be inspected by maintenance teams, American Airlines said.
The incident happened at the same airport where 67 people died in a deadly collision between a jetliner and an Army helicopter in January 2025.
"American Airlines Flight 638 clipped the wing of American Airlines Flight 2152 while taxiing for departure," the FAA said.

Air traffic controllers can be heard on an audio recording saying two Boeing 737s clipped on the airport's runway. The controllers requested an emergency response and fire personnel to the plane, then directed the aircraft to return to the gate.

The "wingtips of both Boeing 737-800s made contact", American Airlines said in a statement. The airline added that it is working to get affected passengers who were evacuated from both planes to their destinations as soon as possible.

A passenger on flight 2152 headed to Chicago's O'Hare airport told the BBC that he felt a "large jolt" on the right side of the aircraft as they were taxiing before departure. The other plane, flight 638, was bound for Dallas-Fort Worth airport.
The passenger added that the "aircraft shook quite violently" upon impact and he heard gasps inside the cabin. He described the moment as "tense", but that nobody seemed to be hurt.
As he looked out the window, he saw a piece of the aircraft on the ground. It looked like the "tip of the wing", he said, describing how the other aircraft's wing was overlapping his plane's wing.
The BBC has contacted American Airlines about reports of the broken wingtip.
As they taxied back to the gate, the passenger said he saw a truck pick up the piece that had fallen.
The fact that this isn't the first incident at this airport was "definitely scary", the passenger said.
Last year, there was a deadly mid-air collision between another American Airlines flight and a military helicopter at Reagan National.
The 64 people on the passenger plane and three US Army members on the Black Hawk helicopter all died in the crash.
The aircraft, en route to land at the DC airport after leaving from Wichita, Kansas, was sent careening into the Potomac River upon impact with the military helicopter.
It was later determined that the helicopter was receiving faulty altitude data, causing it to fly higher than intended.
Reagan National Airport is the smaller of the two DC-area airports and caters mostly to domestic flights.
It sits right near the sprawl of the US capital, the White House and the Pentagon.

Earlier this week, the US Army said it planned to resume helicopter test flights near Reagan airport, according to CBS News, BBC's US News partner. The flights were paused following last year's incident.
BBC has contacted the Pentagon for comment.
